rows.what the ink shows: The initial has a high angular entrance and a broad right bow descending into a long baseline. A short upright/hook and dot precede a flattened joining stroke; the terminal crossed upright, dot and baseline do not recover the compressed internal letters sufficiently to distinguish Introduction from Définition.

Crossing cancellation strokes cover a slanted left loop and a second tall stroke, without the separated paired bars seen in the clear norm below. The lower-right p retains its descending stem and right loop, but the cancelled leading symbol is not securely recoverable.

A small upper loop/blob precedes a long downward-curving stroke with an upturned end, then a dot and a short hooked horizontal group. These sparse strokes do not distinguish the full letter sequence of Quelques from a compressed or abbreviated form.

The opening has a deep narrow loop and a long upper connecting stroke; a separate dotted short upright and low shoulder follow. The remaining two nearly horizontal strokes leave the internal letters and accented ending unresolved.

The first group begins with a short upright and right hook, followed by tiny dots and a long flattened curve. The second begins with a small curved hook and long horizontal join, ending in a dot and two raised shoulders; neither group retains enough distinct bodies for a reliable word reading.
